subject: Recap + action items — feature-level margin, token budget & CAC payback (HealWell)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ng <samantha@healwell.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Recap + action items — feature-level margin, token budget & CAC payback (HealWell)

Hi Samantha — great conversation today, thanks for walking us through the product flows. Quick written recap so we all have the same picture and clear next steps.

High-level discovery (what you told us)
- Pilot scope: 3 customer-facing features for Q3: clinical summarization (visit notes), automated triage routing, and personalized care recommendations.
- Expected pilot cohort: 6k MAU in month 1, ramp to ~40k MAU by month 6.
- Usage profile (approx): 8–12M tokens / month in pilot month range; median session ~320 tokens, heavy tail for long summaries (~2–3k tokens).
- Key economics target from HealWell: maintain feature-level margin >= 40% after inference cost; target CAC payback <= 9 months.

Questions we agreed to confirm
1) Exact monthly token envelope you want us to model for pilot (you mentioned 8–12M; please confirm a mapping to conservative/expected/optimistic).
2) Target price band you expect for a 1M-token unit (you mentioned $/1M target in our call — useful to get a range).
3) Any additional non-inference costs you want treated as part of "feature cost" for the payback calc (e.g., embedding storage, feature infra).

What we’ll deliver by Tue EOD:
- A short per-feature unit-cost sheet: $/1M token scenarios mapped to per-feature $/month at your projected MAU and session lengths. (attached: HealWell_token_profile.xlsx — please update if our session assumptions are off)
- Two pricing options: hosted metered API and a dedicated capacity commitment (3–6 month reserved pool) with illustrative discounts and expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
- A simple CAC-payback demo model that shows how different inference prices and conversion lifts affect payback month.

Immediate asks from you
- Confirm a conservative/expected/optimistic tokens-per-month row we should use (8M / 10M / 14M would work).
- Confirm whether the 9-month CAC payback is a hard constraint or guidance.
- If procurement needs an initial SOW draft or compliance checklist now, loop them in and we’ll prioritize.

Proposed next step
- 30m follow-up next Wed to walk the cost sheet and choose a scenario to model end-to-end for your finance team.

Thanks again — I’ve cc’d Ben and Marissa to keep pricing and customer success aligned.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
<aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Redwood Inference — inference you can operate on

Attachment: HealWell_token_profile.xlsx (xlsx) — usage assumptions & sample session histogram
From: Samantha Ng <samantha@healwell.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@healwell.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + action items — feature-level margin, token budget & CAC payback (HealWell)

Thanks Aisha — very helpful summary and great to have this in writing. Quick answers inline.

On 03 May 2026, Aisha Rahman wrote:
> - Pilot scope: 3 customer-facing features for Q3: clinical summarization (visit notes), automated triage routing, and personalized care recommendations.
Confirmed. Those three are priorities.

> - Expected pilot cohort: 6k MAU in month 1, ramp to ~40k MAU by month 6.
We confirm the ramp but swap numbers: expect 4k MAU month 1 (conservative) -> 35k by month 6 (best estimate). Please model both our conservative and expected.

> - Usage profile (approx): 8–12M tokens / month in pilot month range; median session ~320 tokens, heavy tail for long summaries (~2–3k tokens).
That aligns with our internal telemetry — use 7.5M / 11M / 15M as conservative/expected/optimistic.

> - Key economics target from HealWell: maintain feature-level margin >= 40% after inference cost; target CAC payback <= 9 months.
Both are guidance — margin >= 40% is preferred; CAC payback target is flexible to 6–9 months depending on uplift we can prove.

Action items for Redwood:
- Please share the two pricing scenarios (metered vs reserved) with explicit $/1M token numbers and a worked per-feature cost table.
- Can you include a scenario that assumes 30% LTV uplift from personalization (for payback modeling)?
- Procurement: we’ll need a short SOW draft + SOC2 evidence summary if we move past pilot.

Happy to jump on Wed — I’ll confirm a time after procurement checks availability.

— Samantha
Samantha Ng
Head of Product, HealWell
samantha@healwell.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: HealWell pricing scenarios & payback sketch (for Wed walkthrough)

Aisha/Marissa — putting a quick internal note before we jump on the call with HealWell. Attached is the PDF we’ll share (HealWell_pricing_options_v1.pdf). Key assumptions and two scenarios below.

Assumptions we used (aligns with HealWell):- Tokens per session: median 320, 5% sessions > 2k tokens- Conservative/Expected/Optimistic monthly tokens: 7.5M / 11M / 15M- Target feature margin (HealWell guidance): >= 40%- CAC: HealWell target payback 6–9 months; assume baseline CAC = $600, projected ARPA (post-feature) = $150/year -> need uplift to reach payback thresholds

Scenario A — Hosted metered (fastest time-to-value)- List price: $450 / 1M tokens (metered)- Commercial negotiated pilot band: $320 / 1M tokens (10–25% volume tiers apply)- Per-feature monthly inference cost (expected 11M tokens split as: summarization 45%, triage 30%, recommendations 25%) -> summarization cost = 11M * 0.45 * $320/1M = ~$1,584 / month; triage ~$1,056 / month; recommendations ~$880 / month.- Feature-level margin (assuming $/feature revenue of $4,000/month for summarization, $2,200 for triage, $1,800 for recommendations): summarization margin = (4,000 - 1,584)/4,000 = 60.4%; triage = 52%; recommendations = 51.1% (all above 40%).

Scenario B — Dedicated reserved pool (3-month min commit)- Effective price with reservation and burst: $190 / 1M tokens (with commit + limited burst)- Per-feature monthly inference cost @ 11M tokens -> summarization = 11M*0.45*$190/1M = ~$941; triage ~$627; recommendations ~$522.- Feature-level margin with same revenue assumptions: summarization margin = 76.5%; triage 71.5%; recommendations 71%.

CAC payback sketch- Baseline: ARPA pre-feature = $130/yr. If feature lifts retention/revenue by 20–30% (conservative), ARPA -> $156–169/yr.- Using our commercial pilot pricing (Scenario A at $320/1M) the incremental monthly cost per active customer is small: est $0.22–$0.45/customer/month depending on usage cohort.- With uplift assumptions, payback window moves into 6–9 months for most conservative scenarios; under Dedicated pricing (Scenario B) payback drops toward ~4–6 months because unit inference cost is materially lower.

Recommended items to surface on the Wed call1) Show the per-feature cost table with both pricing scenarios and highlight margin %s.2) Run a sensitivity slide: price per 1M token on x-axis, months-to-payback on y-axis with several uplift assumptions (0%, 20%, 30%).3) Offer a pilot reserved credit: if HealWell commits to 3 months at expected token band (11M/month), we can offer an introductory ECC (early-commit credit) that lowers effective $/1M by another 10% for month 1–2.

I’ll review the PDF and bring the quick sensitivity chart to the demo. If you want different revenue assumptions per feature, flag now and I’ll swap numbers.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: HealWell_pricing_options_v1.pdf (pdf) — includes scenario tables, per-feature cost, and sensitivity charts
